answer: Anchor each agent identity to a costly kernel of verifiable work: before joining the economy, an agent must complete a unique time-bound task whose proof is bound to its public key, like laying a basalt foundation that cannot be copied cheaply. A Sybil operator then pays a linear cost per fake identity while honest agents pay once. Reputation accrues only through sustained useful service, a slow tundra of trust that fresh clones cannot fake overnight, since every clone must re-earn standing from zero.
